title: Scalar-extension tensor associativity on underlying abelian sheaves in independent universes
statement: Let C be a category with Grothendieck topology J, R,S sheaves of commutative rings, $c:R\to S$ a ring-sheaf map, and M an R-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with the ring universe r and module universe max(r,m). Assume J.HasSheafCompose for forgetting commutative rings to rings, weak abelian sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] in universe max(r,m), and that abelian local equivalences are exactly locally bijective maps. There exists a natural isomorphism of functors from S-module sheaves to abelian sheaves: restriction of scalars Res_c [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] followed by tensoring on the right with M followed by forgetting is naturally isomorphic to tensoring on the right with S tensor_R M followed by forgetting, with both tensors and scalar extension given by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No flatness of M or c is required.

proof.text: For each S-module sheaf N use the standard base-change tensor equivalence sectionwise: n tensor m maps to n tensor (1 tensor m), and n tensor (s tensor m) maps back to (s n) tensor m. The pure-tensor formulas commute with restrictions, so these are inverse isomorphisms of underlying abelian presheaves.

The module sheafification unit of the scalar-extension presheaf P=S tensor_R M is locally bijective. Use symmetry to tensor this unit in the first variable and apply the local-bijection tensor sheafification theorem, then symmetry again. This gives an isomorphism after sheafification from N tensor_S P to N tensor_S a(P).

Combine the sectionwise base-change isomorphism and the preceding unit map before sheafification. Their composite is natural in N: on a pure tensor both sides of the naturality equation are f(n) tensor η(1 tensor m). Sheafify this natural transformation of abelian presheaves. Every component is invertible by the preceding two steps, and module sheafification commutes with forgetting to abelian sheaves.
